quotes.text: Users must authenticate payments with their Apple Pay accounts, helping to reduce the risk of fraud or unrecognized payments. However, users can still dispute transactions after they complete payment.
You can submit evidence to contest a dispute directly. The dispute process is the same as that for card payments.
For Visa, liability shift is limited to devices running iOS 16.2 and above. Devices running on iOS versions below 16.2 only receive liability shift on Visa if the card was issued in Europe.
You can partially or fully refund any successful Apple Pay payment. The refund process is the same as that for card payments.

findings: The same canonical URL and title appear in both dated captures (new 1, 5; old 1, 4). The only content.diff hunk changes the Disputes heading by a trailing space (diff 3-8); the new raw adds discovery metadata, accounting for the extra file line. No substantive behavior or qualification changed.

Both captures state Apple Pay authentication does not prevent a completed payment from being disputed, evidence may be submitted directly, and card-payment dispute procedures apply (new 13; old 12). Neither says contesting guarantees a win.

Both captures state major-network liability shift globally, with the Visa exception: iOS 16.2 or later globally and older iOS only if the card was issued in Europe (new 15-17; old 14-16). The page does not prove shift for a particular charge or establish issuer/network adjudication outcome.

Both captures allow full or partial refunds for successful Apple Pay payments under the card refund process (new 19-21; old 18-20). The page gives no refund settlement timing, issuer receipt, or proof of a performed refund.

Current [[source-stripe-apple-pay-disputes-refunds]] captures the central same-URL claims (source 11-21). Its source 17 adds 'via Dashboard' to evidence submission, whereas neither raw line 13 nor old line 12 specifies that UI route; this is a pre-existing unsupported channel detail that can be removed or separately sourced, not a newly observed change.

Those statements match the May capture (old 12, 16, 20) and [[source-stripe-apple-pay-disputes-refunds]] at source 11-21, apart from its unsupported Dashboard-specific phrase.
